Deposited as "Brucella inopinata BO1", which it is not. It sits 0.0234, 0.0237 and 0.0243 (mash, k=21, s=10000) from the three deposited B. inopinata references GCA_030270765.1, GCA_000182725.1 and GCA_900095155.1 - as far as those sit from the classical species - while 0.0011 from B. suis and 0.0012 from B. canis, that is, inside the classical cluster. GCA_000182725.1 carries the same strain name BO1 and is 0.0237 away, so the two assemblies deposited under that strain are not the same organism. match_status=species_match is a false pass: 97.89% ANI to the B. inopinata type clears the 95% threshold because every Brucella is within about 97% of every other, and the check never asks whether another species is closer. The species call is B. canis per Table S5 of Hoover et al. 2026, from Mash, SNP, PubMLST and phylogenetic analysis. Our own evidence establishes only that this is a classical member of the suis-canis group and not B. inopinata: it holds that paper's B. suis assay, which is why the assay shows one exclusion hit on their panel, and its 2-of-10 suis-region profile matches the deposited B. suis GCA_000741995.1, so suis and canis cannot be separated here independently. Checked 2026-10-23.
